Rashi on Gittin 66b:10:1.hebrew: אי כתב ידן הוא - חתימתן הוא דקאמר, והרי חתמו הן:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:10:1.english: If it is their handwriting - [Meaning,] it is their signature that he meant, and behold, they have signed [it].

Rashi on Gittin 66b:10:2.english: Or [is it] the writing of the bill of divorce - and behold, they did not write it:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:11:1.english: Yes, there is a new court - [whose members] have not yet learned to sign:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:12:1.hebrew: ופרכינן ואי סבירא לן כתובו כתב ידן הוא דהוי - הא כתב הגט, אם אמרו לסופר וכתב, כשר, בתמיה:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:12:1.english: And we ask: And if we hold [that] "write" is [a reference to] their signatures - [then] the writing of the bill of divorce, if they told a scribe and he wrote [it], is valid?! [This is asked] in astonishment:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:12:2.hebrew: והאמר שמואל כו' הלכה כר' יוסי - דמתני', וכיון דפריש שמואל טעמא דר"י משום דמילי לא מימסרן לשליח הוא, היאך כשר? הא מילי נינהו! ומשני: אי הוה סבירא לן ופשיטא לן ד"כתובו" דקאמר לא הוי אלא כתב ידן, איכא למימר דכתב הגט, מדלא קפיד עליה, נעשה כאומר "אמרו לסופר ויכתוב", וקס"ד דמודה רבי יוסי באומר "אמרו":
Rashi on Gittin 66b:12:2.english: But didn't Shmuel say, etc., the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - of the Mishnah, and since Shmuel explained Rabbi Yosei's reason as being because [verbal] directives cannot be delegated to an agent, how is [the get] valid? These are [merely verbal] directives! And [the Gemara] answers: If we held and it were clear to us that [when he says] "Write," what he means is only their signatures, we could say that [regarding] the writing of the get, since he is not particular about it, he becomes like one who says, "Tell a scribe to write [it]," and [the Gemara] initially assumed that Rabbi Yosei concedes in [the case of] one who says "Tell [another to write it]":

Rashi on Gittin 66b:13:1.hebrew: ומי מודה - והא אנן תנן: כתב סופר את הגט וחתם עד אחר, כשר:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:13:1.english: And does [Rabbi Yosei] concede - But didn't we learn [in a Mishnah]: [If] a scribe wrote the bill of divorce and another witness signed [it], [it is] valid:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:13:2.hebrew: ואמר ר' ירמיה חתם סופר שנינו - האי "כתב סופר" דקתני, חתם הוא, שאם חתם הסופר בעד ועד אחר עמו, כשר:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:13:2.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya said: We learned "the scribe signed" - This "writing of a scribe" that [the Mishnah] teaches means [his] signature — that if the scribe signed as a witness and another witness [signed] with him, [the get] is valid:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:14:1.hebrew: מתני' - דמכשר חתימת סופר בגט, רבי יוסי היא:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:14:1.english: The Mishnah - which validates the signature of a scribe on a get [bill of divorce], is [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:14:2.hebrew: דאמר מילי לא מימסרן לשליח - הלכך אין אדם חותם בגט אא"כ שמע מפי עצמו, לפי שאין השליח רשאי לומר לעדים: "חתמו בגט פלוני". ומשום הכי ליכא למיחש הכא שמא הבעל לא צוה שיחתום, אלא לשלוחו צוה שיאמר לסופר זה לכתוב ולאחרים לחתום, והשליח חשש שמא יתבייש הסופר לומר "אין מקבלין אותו בעד", ומתוך חששא זו צוה לסופר לחתום. ומהכא שמעינן דבאומר "אמרו" נמי פליג רבי יוסי, דאי סלקא דעתין מודי ביה, היכי מכשר חתימת סופר בגט? נפיק מינה חורבא כו':
Rashi on Gittin 66b:14:2.english: Who said: Verbal directives cannot be delegated to an agent - Therefore, a person may not sign a get unless he heard [the instruction] from [the husband's] own mouth, because the agent is not permitted to say to witnesses, "Sign so-and-so's get." Consequently, there is no concern here that perhaps the husband did not command [the scribe] to sign, but rather commanded his agent to tell this scribe to write [it] and others to sign, and the agent worried that the scribe might be embarrassed, [thinking] they do not accept him as a witness, and out of this concern he commanded the scribe to sign. And from here we learn that Rabbi Yosei also disagrees [in the case] where [the husband] says, "Tell [them to sign]," for if you should think he agrees in that case, how could he validate a scribe's signature on a get? Ruin would come from it, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:1:1.hebrew: או לשלשה (נמי) כתבו ותנו גט לאשתי - אע"פ שהן ראויין ליעשות בית דין, כיון דבהדיא אמר להו "כתבו", לא ב"ד שוינהו אלא עדים:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:1:1.english: Or to three [people] (also), "Write and give a bill of divorce to my wife" - Even though they are fit to be made a court, since he explicitly said to them, "Write," he did not make them a court, but rather witnesses.

Rashi on Gittin 66b:1:2.english: [If] he said to three, "Give" - and he did not say, "Write":

Rashi on Gittin 66b:1:3.hebrew: הרי אלו יאמרו - לעדים אחרים לכתוב ולחתום וליתן, מפני שעשאן ב"ד:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:1:3.english: These [people] should tell - other witnesses to write, sign, and give [it], because he designated them [as] a court:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:2:1.english: From prison - In the name of Rabbi Akiva, who was incarcerated in prison:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:3:1.hebrew: נומינו לשליח - אמרנו לשליח, לחנינא, שנעשה שליח בהלכה זו לאומרה בבית המדרש:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:3:1.english: We said [nomeinu] to the agent - We said to the agent, [that is,] to Chanina, who became an agent for this halakhah to state it in the study hall:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:3:2.hebrew: ילמדו - אם אינם יודעין לכתוב, ילמדו לכתוב עד שיכתבוהו בעצמן:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:3:2.english: They should learn - If they do not know how to write, they should learn to write until they write it themselves:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן אמר לשנים כתבו ותנו גט לאשתי ואמרו לסופר וכתב וחתמו הן מהו - הא דקתני מתניתין "לכתבו בעצמן" — אחתימה קאי, והכא הרי חתמו הן, או דילמא אכתב הגט קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "[If] he said to two [people]: 'Write and give a get to my wife,' and they told a scribe and he wrote [it], and they signed [it], what is [the halakha]?" - That which our Mishnah taught, [that they are] to write [it] themselves — does it refer to the signing, and here they indeed signed [it], or perhaps it refers to the writing of the get:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:2.hebrew: שלח להו תצא - אם ניסת בגט זה, תצא מספק, דמספקא לן אי כשר או לא:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:2.english: He sent to them: She must leave - If she remarried with this bill of divorce, she must leave [her second husband] out of doubt, for we are uncertain whether [it] is valid or not:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:3.hebrew: והדבר צריך תלמוד - כלומר: אין הדבר הזה ברור לנו, וצריכין אנו ללמוד מן הגדולים ממנו אם כשר הוא או לא:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:5:3.english: And the matter requires study - That is to say: this matter is not clear to us, and we must learn from those greater than us whether [the bill of divorce] is valid or not:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:6:1.english: What [is the meaning of] "the matter requires study" - What is Shmuel uncertain about regarding it:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:6:2.hebrew: אי נימא מילי אי מימסרן לשליח - וכשר; ודברים שנאמר לשליח זה, אם יכול למוסרן לשליח אחר:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:6:2.english: If we say [that the question is] whether verbal directives are transferred to an agent - and [thus the bill of divorce is] valid; [that is,] words that were said to this agent, whether he can transfer them to another agent:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:6:3.hebrew: אי לא מימסרן - ופסול, דהכא מילי בעלמא מסר להו ואינן חוזרין ונמסרין לסופר, ולא דמי למוסר גט לשלוחו שיכול לחזור ולעשות שליח אחר:
Rashi on Gittin 66b:6:3.english: [Or] whether they are not transferred - and [the get is therefore] invalid, for here he merely handed over words to them, and they cannot in turn be transferred to a scribe; and it is not comparable to one who hands a get to his agent, who can in turn appoint another agent:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:7:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - of our Mishnah:

Rashi on Gittin 66b:8:1.english: Rather - he [Shmuel] is uncertain whether this "write" that he said to them:

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:10:1.hebrew: כתב ידן הוא או כתב הגט הוא - אע"ג דלא נפקא מינה מידי, דאידי ואידי מילי נינהו ולא ממסרן לשליח, הא מסיק דלשמואל אמר "אמרו" כשר, וא"כ "חתם סופר ועד" פסול, דהא בהא תליא, כדאמרינן בסמוך. וכשאומר לשנים "כתבו ותנו", הוי כאילו אמר להם בפירוש שישתפו אחר עמהם לכתוב או לחתום; לכך בעי מה רוצה הבעל שיעשו הם. ולקמן דאמר "אי סבירא לן ד'כתבו' כתב ידן הוא, הא כתב הגט כו'", הוא הדין דהוה מצי למימר אפכא: "אי סבירא לן דכתב הגט הוא, כתב ידן כשר":
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:10:1.english: Is it their handwriting, or is it the writing of the bill of divorce? - Even though no [practical difference] emerges from it, since both this and that are [mere] verbal directives and cannot be delegated to an agent, nevertheless, [the Gemara] concludes that according to Shmuel, [if he] said, "Tell [someone else]," it is valid, and if so, [a bill of divorce where] "a scribe signed and [one] witness [signed]" is invalid, for this depends on that, as we say immediately below. And when he says to two [people], "Write and give," it is as if he explicitly told them to include another [person] with them to write or to sign; therefore, [Shmuel] asks what the husband wants them to do [themselves]. And below, where [the Gemara] says, "If we hold that 'Write' means their handwriting, then the writing of the bill of divorce [is valid], etc." — the same applies that it could have said the reverse: "If we hold that it means the writing of the bill of divorce, [then] their handwriting is valid":

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:12:1.hebrew: הא כתב הגט כשר כו' - וא"ת: ומאי קשיא ליה מהא דמילי לא מימסרן לשליח? הא לר"מ, אפי' מצאו באשפה כשר! וי"ל: דשמואל פוסק הלכה כר' אלעזר, ול"ל דר"מ; ולפ"ז ר' יוסי דמתני' נמי כר"א. א"נ: נהי דמכשר ר"מ כשמצאו הבעל באשפה, היכא שצוה לכתוב מודה ר"מ שצריך לעשות צוויו; ואפילו כתב ידן הוא, הוי כאילו צוה להדיא שיאמר לסופר שיכתוב, ולא סגי הכא במצאו באשפה אפילו לר"מ:
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:12:1.english: Is [the] writing of the bill of divorce valid, etc. - And if you ask: What is [the Gemara's] difficulty from that [principle] that verbal directives cannot be delegated to an agent? Why, according to Rabbi Meir, even if he found it in a garbage heap it is valid! One can answer: Shmuel rules [that the] halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, and he does not hold [the view] of Rabbi Meir; and according to this, Rabbi Yosei of our Mishnah also [holds] like Rabbi Elazar. Alternatively: although Rabbi Meir validates [a get] when the husband found it in a garbage heap, where he commanded [them] to write [it], Rabbi Meir agrees that his command must be carried out; and even [if "write"] is [a reference to] their signatures, it is as if he explicitly commanded that he tell a scribe to write [it], and finding it in a garbage heap does not suffice here even according to Rabbi Meir:

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:13:1.hebrew: חתם סופר שנינו - וא"ת: הא שמואל גופיה קאמר בפרק בתרא (לקמן גיטין דף פו:) ד"כתב סופר ועד" שנינו, ואתיא מתניתין אפילו כר"מ, דלא נפיק מיניה שום חורבא; א"כ מאי פריך ליה הכא לשמואל? וי"ל: דנהי דפליג בפירוש דמתניתין ד"כתב סופר ועד", במילתיה דר' יוסי לא אשכחן דפליג אדרב חסדא ורבי ירמיה, אי מודה ר' יוסי באומר "אמרו" אי לאו. ובפרק מי שאחזו (לקמן גיטין דף עב.) דייקינן מברייתא לאפוקי ממאן דאמר מודה רבי יוסי באומר "אמרו":
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:13:1.english: We learned "the scribe signed" - And if you say: Behold, Shmuel himself says in the last chapter (below, Gittin 86b) that we learned "the scribe wrote and a witness [signed]," and [thus] the Mishnah accords even with Rabbi Meir, for no harm comes out of it; if so, why does [the Gemara] raise a difficulty here against Shmuel? And one can say: Although he disagrees regarding the explanation of the Mishnah of "the scribe wrote and a witness [signed]," regarding the matter of Rabbi Yosei we have not found that he disagrees with Rav Chisda and Rabbi Yirmeya as to whether Rabbi Yosei concedes in [the case of] one who says "Tell [another to write it]" or not. And in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (below, Gittin 72a), we infer from a baraita to exclude the one who says that Rabbi Yosei concedes in [the case of] one who says "Tell [another to write it]":

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:14:1.hebrew: מתניתין מני רבי יוסי היא דאמר מילי לא מימסרן לשליח - אפילו באומר לשלשה "תנו", הוא הדין באומר "אמרו", ולהכי לא נפקא מינה חורבא. אבל לר"מ, דאמר מילי מימסרן לשליח באומר לשלשה "תנו", כ"ש באומר "אמרו" דכשר; ולהכי לדידיה, "חתם סופר ועד" פסול, דלא ליתי לידי חורבא. ולמאי דמסיק נמי באומר "אמרו" כשר ולא תעשה ולא שכיחא, מ"מ לא מתוקמא מתניתין דמכשיר "חתם סופר ועד" כרבי מאיר, דחיישינן לדידיה לתקלה אחריתי: דזימנין דאמר לשלשה "תנו", ונמלכו שלשתן לומר לסופר לכתוב ולפלוני ופלוני לחתום, ואזלי תרתי מינייהו מדעת שלשתן ואמרו לסופר וכתב, ומשום כיסופא דסופר מחתמי ליה בלא ידיעת שלישי. והא שכיחא, דכשאומר לשלשה "תנו", אומרים לאחרים שיכתבו ויתנו לכתחילה, כדתנן במתני', ולא חיישינן שמא תשכור עדים כי אמר לג' "תנו", דכיון דאומר "אמרו" כשר ולא תעשה, לא יחתום הסופר אם לא שידע בודאי שעשאן הבעל ב"ד. ואם תאמר: כיון דלר"מ "חתם סופר ועד" פסול, היכי תנן "אמר לשנים תנו, הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו, דברי ר' מאיר"? ויש לומר דלר' מאיר: כיון דחתם סופר פסול, הו"ל כאומר "אמרו לסופר ויכתוב, ואתם חתמו", ו"הרי אלו יכתבו" היינו יחתומו. ואם תאמר: אכתי היכי קתני "הרי אלו יכתבו ויתנו" לכתחלה? למאי דאמר בסמוך, הא נמי כשר ולא תעשה! ותירץ רבינו תם דמשום דאמר לשלשה, שהוא לכתחלה, נקט האי לישנא דיכתבו ויתנו. אי נמי הכי קאמר: אם באו לקיים שליחותם, יכתבו ויתנו בעצמן, דאי אמרי לאחריני ועבדי, אפי' דיעבד לא מהני. אי נמי דזימנין דתעשה אפי' לכתחלה, כגון בשעת הדחק:
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:14:1.english: Whose opinion is expressed in the mishna? It is that of Rabbi Yosei, who said: Verbal directives cannot be delegated to an agent - Even when one says to three [people], "Give [a bill of divorce]," the same applies when one says, "Tell [others to write and sign]," and therefore no pitfall results from it. However, according to Rabbi Meir, who says that verbal directives can be delegated to an agent when one says to three [people], "Give," all the more so when one says, "Tell," it is valid; and therefore, according to him, [a bill of divorce in which] "the scribe signed and a witness [signed]" is invalid, so that it does not come to a pitfall. And even according to what [the Gemara] concludes, that when one says, "Tell," it is valid [after the fact] yet "it shall not be done," and [therefore] it is uncommon, nevertheless the mishna that validates "the scribe signed and a witness [signed]" cannot be established as following Rabbi Meir, because according to him we are concerned about another pitfall: for sometimes one says to three [people], "Give," and the three of them decide to tell a scribe to write and so-and-so and so-and-so to sign, and two of them go with the knowledge of all three and tell the scribe and he writes [it], and because of the scribe's embarrassment, they have him sign without the knowledge of the third [agent]. And this [case] is common, for when one says to three [people], "Give," they tell others to write and give [the bill of divorce] ab initio, as we learned in the mishna; and we are not concerned lest she hire witnesses when he said to three, "Give," for since saying "Tell" is valid [only after the fact, as] "it shall not be done," the scribe will not sign unless he knows for certain that the husband made them a court. And if you say: Since according to Rabbi Meir, "the scribe signed and a witness [signed]" is invalid, how is it taught [in the mishna]: "[If] he said to two, 'Give,' these should write and give [it]; [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir"? One can say that according to Rabbi Meir, since "the scribe signed" is invalid, it is as if he said, "Tell a scribe and he will write, and you sign," and "these should write" means they should sign. And if you say: Still, how does it teach "these should write and give" ab initio? According to what [the Gemara] says immediately below, this too is "valid, yet it shall not be done"! And Rabbeinu Tam answered that because [the mishna also] speaks of one who said to three, which is ab initio, it used this wording of "they should write and give." Alternatively, this is what it is saying: if they come to fulfill their agency, they must write and give [it] themselves, for if they tell others and [those others] do it, even after the fact it is not effective. Alternatively, sometimes it may be done even ab initio, such as in a time of pressing need:

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:5:1.hebrew: אמר לשנים כתבו ותנו גט כו' ואמרו לסופר וכתב וחתמו הן מהו - הוה מצי למיבעי באומר לשנים "תנו" בלא "כתבו", ד"תנו" לשנים בלא "כתבו" כ"כתבו ותנו" דמי; ושמא נקט "כתבו ותנו" לרבותא:
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:5:1.english: He said to two [people], "Write and give a bill of divorce, etc.," and they told the scribe and he wrote [it] and they signed, what is [the halakha]? - [The Gemara] could have asked about [one who] says to two [people], "Give," without "Write," for "Give" to two [people] without "Write" is equivalent to "Write and give"; and perhaps it stated "Write and give" for the sake of a greater novelty:

Tosafot on Gittin 66b:7:1.hebrew: והאמר שמואל אמר רבי הלכה כרבי יוסי - והוא הדין דהוה מצי למיפרך מדשמואל דפרק כל הגט (לעיל גיטין דף כט.), דאמר: מתנה הרי היא כגט, דמילי לא מימסרן לשליח. אבל ממתני', דאפי' רבי מאיר מודה באומר לשנים "תנו" או לשלשה אומר "כתבו ותנו", לא מצי למיפרך; דה"א דטעמא משום בזיון דבעל, כדאמר אביי בפרק כל הגט (גז"ש), והוה אמינא דבכתיבה ליכא בזיון, אלא בחתימה דאיכא פרסום טפי:
Tosafot on Gittin 66b:7:1.english: But didn't Shmuel say that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - Likewise, [the Gemara] could have raised an objection from [the statement of] Shmuel in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (above, Gittin 29a), who said [that] a gift is like a bill of divorce, in that verbal directives cannot be delegated to an agent. However, from the Mishnah — where even Rabbi Meir concedes when [a husband] says to two [people], "Give [a bill of divorce]," or to three [people] he says, "Write and give [it]" — [the Gemara] could not have raised an objection; for one might have said that the reason [they cannot delegate] is due to the husband's disgrace, as Abaye says in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (ibid.), and one might have said that in writing [the text] there is no disgrace, only in signing, where there is greater publicity:
